description: The bar chart is intended to show, for each of four QA datasets, how many questions (out of 40) have at least one factual error in GPT‑3 chain-of-thought outputs under three different methods. The category axis is the horizontal axis, listing the datasets HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC from left to right. The value axis is the vertical axis with a linear scale from 0 to 40, labeled by numeric ticks at regular 5-unit intervals. Each dataset has a grouped set of three bars arranged side-by-side, with the legend indicating orange/yellow for “NoR QA,” red with a dotted pattern for “OneR QA,” and dark blue with diagonal hatching for “IRCoT QA”; numeric value labels are printed above each bar. For HotpotQA, the bars are approximately 15 (NoR QA), 10 (OneR QA), and 5 (IRCoT QA). For 2WikiMQA, the bars are approximately 29 (NoR QA), 23 (OneR QA), and 14 (IRCoT QA). For MuSiQue, the bars are approximately 28 (NoR QA), 27 (OneR QA), and 23 (IRCoT QA). For IIRC, the bars are approximately 15 (NoR QA), 14 (OneR QA), and 11 (IRCoT QA). The datasets appear in a fixed left-to-right order rather than being sorted by bar height, and no bars are specially emphasized beyond the distinct colors/patterns and the displayed value annotations.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT-3 using different methods contains at least one factual error. The horizontal axis presents the categories labeled as 'HotpotQA,' '2WikiMQA,' 'MuSiQue,' and 'IIRC,' ordered from left to right. The vertical axis represents the number of factual errors, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40, marked at intervals of 5. Each category includes three grouped bars, each colored differently: yellow for 'NoR QA,' red with dots for 'OneR QA,' and blue with diagonal lines for 'IRCoT QA,' as indicated by the legend. For 'HotpotQA,' the bars indicate values of approximately 15, 10, and 5 for 'NoR QA,' 'OneR QA,' and 'IRCoT QA,' respectively. In '2WikiMQA,' the values are roughly 29, 23, and 18, showing a notable decline in errors for 'IRCoT QA.' In 'MuSiQue,' the values are around 28, 27, and 23, with 'OneR QA' slightly exceeding 'NoR QA.' Finally, 'IIRC' demonstrates values of 15, 14, and 11, with 'NoR QA' showing a consistent lead over the other methods across all datasets. Overall, 'NoR QA' consistently outperforms 'OneR QA' and 'IRCoT QA' in minimizing factual errors across all datasets, with the most significant improvement observed in '2WikiMQA.'
